verses.1:1: In the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD from the mouth of Jeremiah would be completed, the LORD roused the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, and he had a proclamation go out throughout all his kingdom, and in writing as well, saying,
verses.1:2: "This is what Cyrus, king of Persia, says: All the kingdoms of the earth the LORD, the God of heaven, has given to me, and He has commissioned me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
verses.1:3: Anyone among you from all His people—may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and let him build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel; He is the God who is in Jerusalem.
verses.1:4: And every survivor from all the places where he sojourns—let the men of his place support him with silver and with gold, with goods and with livestock, along with the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem."
verses.1:5: And the heads of the ancestral houses of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites, arose—everyone whose spirit God had roused—to go up to build the house of the LORD that is in Jerusalem.
verses.1:6: And all those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with livestock, and with costly gifts, in addition to everything that was offered freely.
verses.1:7: And King Cyrus brought out the vessels of the house of the LORD, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his gods.
verses.1:8: Cyrus, king of Persia, brought them out through the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and he counted them over to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
verses.1:9: And this was their count: thirty gold basins, one thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives;
verses.1:10: thirty gold bowls, four hundred ten secondary silver bowls, and one thousand other vessels.
verses.1:11: All the vessels of gold and of silver totaled five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought up all of them when the exiled community was brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
verses.2:1: And these are the people of the province who went up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had exiled to Babylon, and they returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each man to his city.
verses.2:2: Those who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah—the count of the men of the people of Israel:
verses.2:3: The sons of Parosh: two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
verses.2:4: The sons of Shephatiah: three hundred seventy-two.
verses.2:5: The sons of Arah: seven hundred seventy-five.
verses.2:6: The sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab: two thousand eight hundred twelve.
verses.2:7: The sons of Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:8: The sons of Zattu: nine hundred forty-five.
verses.2:9: The sons of Zaccai: seven hundred sixty.
verses.2:10: The sons of Bani: six hundred forty-two.
verses.2:11: The sons of Bebai: six hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:12: The sons of Azgad: one thousand two hundred twenty-two.
verses.2:13: The sons of Adonikam: six hundred sixty-six.
verses.2:14: The sons of Bigvai: two thousand fifty-six.
verses.2:15: The sons of Adin: four hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:16: The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah: ninety-eight.
verses.2:17: The sons of Bezai: three hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:18: The sons of Jorah: one hundred twelve.
verses.2:19: The sons of Hashum: two hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:21: The sons of Bethlehem: one hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:23: The men of Anathoth: one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.2:25: The sons of Kiriath-arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: seven hundred forty-three.
verses.2:26: The sons of Ramah and Geba: six hundred twenty-one.
verses.2:27: The men of Michmas: one hundred twenty-two.
verses.2:28: The men of Bethel and Ai: two hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:30: The sons of Magbish: one hundred fifty-six.
verses.2:31: The sons of the other Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:32: The sons of Harim: three hundred twenty.
verses.2:33: The sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono: seven hundred twenty-five.
verses.2:34: The sons of Jericho: three hundred forty-five.
verses.2:35: The sons of Senaah: three thousand six hundred thirty.
verses.2:36: The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua—nine hundred seventy-three.
verses.2:37: The sons of Immer: one thousand fifty-two.
verses.2:38: The sons of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
verses.2:39: The sons of Harim: one thousand seventeen.
verses.2:40: The Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodaviah—seventy-four.
verses.2:41: The singers: the sons of Asaph—one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.2:42: The sons of the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, and the sons of Shobai; in all, one hundred thirty-nine.
verses.2:43: The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
verses.2:44: the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padon,
verses.2:45: the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub,
verses.2:46: the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shalmai, the sons of Hanan,
verses.2:47: the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Reaiah,
verses.2:48: the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam,
verses.2:49: the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Besai,
verses.2:50: the sons of Asnah, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephusim,
verses.2:51: the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
verses.2:52: the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
verses.2:53: the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
verses.2:54: the sons of Neziah, and the sons of Hatipha.
verses.2:55: The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Hassophereth, the sons of Peruda,
verses.2:56: the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
verses.2:57: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, and the sons of Ami.
verses.2:58: All the temple servants and the sons of the servants of Solomon: three hundred ninety-two.
verses.2:59: And these are those who went up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, yet they could not declare their fathers' house and their lineage, whether they were from Israel:
verses.2:60: The sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, and the sons of Nekoda: six hundred fifty-two.
verses.2:61: And from the sons of the priests: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, and the sons of Barzillai, who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called after their name.
verses.2:62: These searched for their written record among those enrolled by genealogy, but they were not found, so they were disqualified from the priesthood as unclean.
verses.2:63: And the governor told them that they were not to eat from the most holy things until a priest arose with Urim and Thummim.
verses.2:64: The entire assembly altogether was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
verses.2:65: apart from their male servants and their female servants—these were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven—and they had two hundred male singers and female singers.
verses.2:66: Their horses: seven hundred thirty-six; their mules: two hundred forty-five.
verses.2:67: Their camels: four hundred thirty-five; donkeys: six thousand seven hundred twenty.
verses.2:68: And some of the heads of the fathers' houses, upon coming to the house of the LORD, which is in Jerusalem, gave freewill offerings for the house of God to raise it up on its foundation.
verses.2:69: According to their means, they gave to the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand gold darics, five thousand silver minas, and one hundred priests' tunics.
verses.2:70: And the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants settled in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.
verses.3:1: When the seventh month arrived and the sons of Israel were in the cities, the people assembled as one man to Jerusalem.
verses.3:2: Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers the priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, rose up and built the altar of the God of Israel to offer up burnt offerings on it, as is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
verses.3:3: They established the altar upon its bases, for dread was upon them from the peoples of the lands, and they offered up burnt offerings on it to the LORD, burnt offerings for the morning and for the evening.
verses.3:4: They observed the Feast of Booths as is written, and offered the burnt offering of each day by number, according to the ordinance, each day's portion on its day,
verses.3:5: and after that the continual burnt offering, and those for the new moons and for all the consecrated appointed times of the LORD, and for everyone who freely offered a freewill offering to the LORD.
verses.3:6: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer up burnt offerings to the LORD, yet the temple of the LORD had not been founded.
verses.3:7: And they gave silver to the stonecutters and the craftsmen, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians, to bring cedar timbers from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the authorization of Cyrus king of Persia for them.
verses.3:8: In the second year of their coming to the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak, with the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites and all who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem, made a start; and they appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to direct the work of the house of the LORD.
verses.3:9: Then Jeshua, with his sons and his brothers, and Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, stood as one to direct those doing the work in the house of God, together with the sons of Henadad, their sons and their brothers, the Levites.
verses.3:10: When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, they stationed the priests, robed, with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the order of David king of Israel.
verses.3:11: And they sang responsively in praising and giving thanks to the LORD, "For He is good, for His loyal love is forever upon Israel." And all the people gave a great shout in praising the LORD because the house of the LORD had been founded.
verses.3:12: Yet many of the priests and the Levites and the heads of the fathers' houses, the old men who had seen the first house, were weeping with a loud voice when this house was founded before their eyes, while many lifted up their voice with shouting in joy,
verses.3:13: so that the people could not discern the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the weeping of the people, because the people were raising a great shout, and the sound was heard far off.
verses.4:1: Now the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the exile were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.4:2: So they came near to Zerubbabel and to the heads of the fathers' houses and said to them, "Let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and to Him we have been sacrificing from the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here."
verses.4:3: But Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel said to them, "It is not for you and us to build a house for our God; rather, we together will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, king of Persia, commanded us."
verses.4:4: Then the people of the land kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah and terrifying them from building,
verses.4:5: and hiring counselors against them to thwart their counsel all the days of Cyrus king of Persia and until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
verses.4:6: And during the reign of Ahasuerus, at the outset of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the residents of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.4:7: And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the text of the letter was written in Aramaic and translated into Aramaic.
verses.4:8: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows:
verses.4:9: Then Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates, the Dinaites and the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Dehaites, the Elamites,
verses.4:10: and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and the rest of Beyond the River, and now.
verses.4:11: This is the copy of the letter that they sent to him: "To King Artaxerxes: Your servants, the men of Beyond the River, and now.
verses.4:12: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you have come to us at Jerusalem; they are building the rebellious and wicked city, and they are completing the walls and repairing the foundations.
verses.4:13: Now let it be known to the king that if this city is built and the walls are completed, they will not pay tribute, tax, or toll, and in the end it will bring loss to kings.
verses.4:14: Now, since we eat the salt of the palace and it is not proper for us to see the king's dishonor, for this reason we have sent and informed the king,
verses.4:15: so that a search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. And you will find in the book of the records and know that this city is a rebellious city, bringing loss to kings and provinces, and that they have practiced sedition within it from ancient days; for this reason this city was devastated.
verses.4:16: We are informing the king that if this city is built and the walls are completed, because of this you will have no portion in Beyond the River."
verses.4:17: The king sent a reply to Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria, and to the rest of Beyond the River: "Peace, and now.
verses.4:18: The letter that you sent to us has been read distinctly before me.
verses.4:19: And by me a decree was issued, and they searched and found that from ancient days this city has risen up against kings, and rebellion and sedition have been practiced in it.
verses.4:20: And mighty kings have been over Jerusalem, exercising dominion over all of Beyond the River, and tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.
verses.4:21: Now issue a decree to halt those men, and this city shall not be built until a decree is issued from me.
verses.4:22: And be careful not to act negligently regarding this; why should harm increase to bring loss to kings?"
verses.4:23: Then, once the copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their associates, they went in haste to Jerusalem, to the Jews, and halted them with force and power.
verses.4:24: At that time the work of the house of God that is in Jerusalem halted, and it remained halted until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
verses.5:1: Now Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and in Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
verses.5:2: At that time Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak rose up and began to build the house of God that is in Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, assisting them.
verses.5:3: At that very time Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their associates came to them and spoke to them in this way: "Who issued a decree for you to build this house and to complete this structure?"
verses.5:4: Then we spoke to them as follows: "What are the names of the men who are building this building?"
verses.5:5: But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, and they did not halt them until the report should go to Darius, and then a letter should be sent back concerning this.
verses.5:6: The copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his associates, the Apharsachites who were in Beyond the River, sent to King Darius.
verses.5:7: They sent a report to him, and within it was written as follows: "To King Darius, all peace.
verses.5:8: Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with massive stones, and timber is being set in the walls; and this work is being performed diligently and is prospering in their hands.
verses.5:9: Then we questioned those elders; we spoke to them as follows: 'Who issued a decree for you to build this house and to complete this structure?'
verses.5:10: Moreover, we asked them for their names to make them known to you, so that we might record the names of the men who were at their head.
verses.5:11: And they returned this answer to us, saying, 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the house that had been built many years before this, and a great king of Israel built it and completed it.
verses.5:12: Yet because our fathers provoked the God of heaven to anger, He gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean; and he tore down this house and deported the people to Babylon.
verses.5:13: Nevertheless, in the first year of Cyrus the king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree for this house of God to be built.
verses.5:14: Moreover, King Cyrus brought out from the temple of Babylon the vessels of the house of God, of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from the temple that was in Jerusalem and carried to the temple of Babylon, and they were given to one named Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.
verses.5:15: And he said to him, "Take these vessels; go, deposit them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be built on its site."
verses.5:16: Then that Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God that is in Jerusalem, and from that time to the present it has been under construction, and it is not completed.'
verses.5:17: And now, if it is pleasing to the king, let a search be made in the treasure house of the king there in Babylon, whether it is so that a decree was issued by King Cyrus to build that house of God in Jerusalem; and let the king send us his will concerning this."
verses.6:1: Then King Darius issued a decree, and they searched in the house of the records where they deposited the treasures in Babylon.
verses.6:2: And in Ecbatana, in the citadel which is in the province of Media, a scroll was found, and inside it a memorandum was written as follows:
verses.6:3: "In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decree: Concerning the house of God in Jerusalem, let the house be built, the place where they offer sacrifices, and let its foundations be laid, its height sixty cubits, its width sixty cubits,
verses.6:4: three courses of massive stones and a course of new timber; and let the expense be paid from the king's house.
verses.6:5: Also let the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar brought out from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, be restored, and let each go to the temple in Jerusalem, to its place, and you shall deposit them in the house of God."
verses.6:6: "Now, Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their colleagues, the Apharsachites who are in Beyond the River, stay far away from there.
verses.6:7: Leave the work of that house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build that house of God on its site.
verses.6:8: Moreover, a decree is issued by me concerning what you shall do for those elders of the Jews for the building of that house of God: from the king's resources, namely the tribute of Beyond the River, the expense shall be paid in full to those men without interruption.
verses.6:9: And whatever is needed—young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, and wheat, salt, wine, and oil—according to the word of the priests who are in Jerusalem, let it be given to them day by day without fail,
verses.6:10: so that they may offer pleasing offerings to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
verses.6:11: Also a decree is issued by me that if any man alters this edict, let a timber be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and impaled upon it, and let his house be made a refuse heap on account of this.
verses.6:12: And may the God who caused His name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who stretches out his hand to alter this or to destroy that house of God which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued a decree; let it be carried out with full diligence."
verses.6:13: Then Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their colleagues carried it out with full diligence, just as King Darius had sent word.
verses.6:14: And the elders of the Jews kept building and prospering through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. And they built and completed it by the decree of the God of Israel and by the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
verses.6:15: And this house was finished by the third day of the month of Adar, which was the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
verses.6:16: And the sons of Israel—the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the people of the exile—observed the dedication of this house of God with joy.
verses.6:17: And they offered for the dedication of this house of God one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering for all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
verses.6:18: And they appointed the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their orders for the service of God in Jerusalem, according to what is written in the book of Moses.
verses.6:19: And the people of the exile observed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.6:20: For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves as one; all of them were pure. So they slaughtered the Passover offering for all the people of the exile, for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
verses.6:21: And the sons of Israel who had returned from the exile ate it, along with everyone who had separated himself from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to join them, to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.6:22: And they observed the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with gladness, for the LORD had made them glad and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God of Israel.
verses.7:1: Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
verses.7:2: son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
verses.7:3: son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
verses.7:4: son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
verses.7:5: son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest,
verses.7:6: this Ezra went up from Babylon; he was a skilled scribe in the law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given. And the king gave him his entire request, since the hand of the LORD his God was upon him.
verses.7:7: And some of the sons of Israel and some of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
verses.7:8: And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was the seventh year of the king.
verses.7:9: For on the first day of the first month was the beginning of the journey up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, since the good hand of his God was upon him.
verses.7:10: For Ezra had directed his heart to search the law of the LORD and to do it, and to teach statute and ordinance in Israel.
verses.7:11: Now this is the copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe—a scribe of the words of the commandments of the LORD and His statutes for Israel:
verses.7:12: "Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven: full greetings. And now,
verses.7:13: a decree is issued by me that anyone in my kingdom from the people of Israel, and its priests and the Levites, who volunteers to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
verses.7:14: For you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of your God which is in your hand,
verses.7:15: and to bring silver and gold which the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
verses.7:16: and all the silver and gold that you find in all the province of Babylon, along with the freewill offering of the people and the priests, freely offered for the house of their God which is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:17: Therefore, with full diligence you shall buy with this money bulls, rams, and lambs, together with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and you shall offer them upon the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:18: And whatever seems good to you and to your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, you may do according to the will of your God.
verses.7:19: And the vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full before the God of Jerusalem.
verses.7:20: And the rest of what is needed for the house of your God, which it falls to you to provide, you may provide from the king's treasure house.
verses.7:21: And by me, even I, King Artaxerxes, a decree is issued to all the treasurers who are in Beyond the River, that whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, asks of you shall be done with full diligence,
verses.7:22: up to one hundred talents of silver, up to one hundred kors of wheat, up to one hundred baths of wine, up to one hundred baths of oil, and salt without a prescribed limit.
verses.7:23: Whatever is by the decree of the God of heaven, let it be done zealously for the house of the God of heaven, for why should there be wrath against the kingdom of the king and his sons?
verses.7:24: We also make known to you that it is not permitted to impose tribute, tax, or toll upon any of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the temple servants, or the attendants of this house of God.
verses.7:25: And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God which is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges who shall judge all the people who are in Beyond the River—all who know the laws of your God—and you shall instruct anyone who does not know them.
verses.7:26: And anyone who will not observe the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be strictly executed upon him, whether for death, or for banishment, or for confiscation of property, or for imprisonment."
verses.7:27: Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who placed something like this in the king's heart, to beautify the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem,
verses.7:28: and who extended loyal love to me before the king and his counselors and before all the king's mighty officials. And I gained strength, since the hand of the LORD my God was upon me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
verses.8:1: And these are the heads of their fathers' houses and their genealogical registration, those who went up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:
verses.8:2: From the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; from the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; from the sons of David, Hattush.
verses.8:3: From the sons of Shecaniah; from the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him one hundred fifty males were registered by genealogy.
verses.8:4: From the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males.
verses.8:5: From the sons of Shecaniah, son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred males.
verses.8:6: And from the sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males.
verses.8:7: And from the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males.
verses.8:8: And from the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty males.
verses.8:9: From the sons of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred eighteen males.
verses.8:10: And from the sons of Shelomith, son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred sixty males.
verses.8:11: And from the sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight males.
verses.8:12: And from the sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred ten males.
verses.8:13: And from the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, and these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah; and with them sixty males.
verses.8:14: And from the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with him seventy males.
verses.8:15: Then I gathered them to the river that flows to Ahava, and we camped there for three days. When I examined the people and the priests, I did not find any of the sons of Levi there.
verses.8:16: And I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, leaders, and for Joiarib and Elnathan, men of understanding.
verses.8:17: And I commanded them to go to Iddo the leader at the place Casiphia, and I put words in their mouths to speak to Iddo, his brother, and the temple servants at the place Casiphia, to bring us ministers for the house of our God.
verses.8:18: And they brought us, according to the good hand of our God upon us, a man of insight from the sons of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Israel, namely Sherebiah, with his sons and his brothers, eighteen;
verses.8:19: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah from the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty;
verses.8:20: and from the temple servants whom David and the officials had given for the service of the Levites, two hundred twenty temple servants; all of them were listed by name.
verses.8:21: So I proclaimed a fast there by the river Ahava, to humble ourselves before our God and seek from Him a straight way for us, for our little ones, and for all our possessions.
verses.8:22: For I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to help us against an enemy on the way, because we had spoken to the king, saying, "The hand of our God is upon all who seek Him for good, and His might and His wrath are against all who forsake Him."
verses.8:23: So we fasted and sought our God about this, and He responded to our plea.
verses.8:24: Then I set apart twelve from the leaders of the priests, Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and with them ten of their brothers.
verses.8:25: I weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the vessels, the contribution for the house of our God that the king, his counselors, his officials, and all Israel who were present had contributed.
verses.8:26: Thus I weighed into their hands six hundred fifty talents of silver, silver vessels weighing one hundred talents, one hundred talents of gold;
verses.8:27: and twenty gold bowls valued at one thousand darics, and two vessels of fine burnished bronze, as precious as gold.
verses.8:28: And I told them, "You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are a voluntary offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.
verses.8:29: Keep watch and guard them until you weigh them out before the leaders of the priests and the Levites, and the leaders of the fathers' houses of Israel in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD."
verses.8:30: So the priests and the Levites received the weighed silver, gold, and vessels to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.
verses.8:31: Then we set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem; and the hand of our God was upon us, and He rescued us from the grip of the enemy and those lying in ambush along the way.
verses.8:32: So we arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.
verses.8:33: On the fourth day, the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed out in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest, and with him was Eleazar son of Phinehas; and with them were Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui, the Levites.
verses.8:34: All of it was by number and by weight, and the entire weight was written down at that time.
verses.8:35: Those who came from the captivity, the sons of the exile, presented burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering, all of it a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.8:36: And they delivered the king's decrees to the king's satraps and the governors of Beyond the River, and they gave support to the people and the house of God.
verses.9:1: When these things were finished, the officials came near to me, saying, "The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands regarding their abominations, those of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
verses.9:2: For they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, so the holy seed has intermingled with the peoples of the lands. And the hand of the officials and the deputies has been first in this unfaithfulness."
verses.9:3: When I heard this matter, I tore my garment and my cloak, plucked some of the hair of my head and my beard, and sat down stunned.
verses.9:4: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered to me over the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat stunned until the evening offering.
verses.9:5: And at the evening offering I rose from my fasting, with my garment and my cloak torn, and I knelt on my knees and spread out my palms to the LORD my God.
verses.9:6: And I said, "My God, I am ashamed and humiliated to lift my face to You, my God, for our iniquities have multiplied above our heads, and our guilt has grown up to the heavens.
verses.9:7: From the days of our fathers until this day we have been in great guilt; and because of our iniquities, we, our kings, and our priests have been handed over into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to shame of face, as it is today.
verses.9:8: Yet now, for a short moment, favor has come from the LORD our God to leave us an escaped remnant and to give us a peg in His holy place, so that our God may give light to our eyes and give us a little reviving in our slavery.
verses.9:9: For we are slaves, yet in our slavery our God has not forsaken us; instead, He has extended loyal love to us in the presence of the kings of Persia, to give us reviving, to raise up the house of our God and restore its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.9:10: And now, what can we say, our God, after this? For we have forsaken Your commandments,
verses.9:11: which You commanded by the hand of Your servants the prophets, saying, 'The land you are entering to possess is a land of impurity through the impurity of the peoples of the lands, with their abominations by which they have filled it from one end to the other with their uncleanness.
verses.9:12: Therefore now, do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or their well-being, so that you may grow strong, eat the good of the land, and pass it on as an inheritance to your sons forever.'
verses.9:13: And after all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt, since You, our God, have held back, punishing us less than our iniquity deserves, and have given us an escaped remnant like this,
verses.9:14: should we break Your commandments once more and intermarry with the peoples of these abominations? Would You not be angry with us to the point of complete destruction, so that there would be no remnant or survivor?
verses.9:15: LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous, for we have been left as an escaped remnant, as it is today. Here we are before You in our guilt, for no one is able to stand before You on account of this."
verses.10:1: Now as Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and throwing himself down in front of the house of God, a very large assembly gathered to him from Israel, men, women, and children, for the people wept with great weeping.
verses.10:2: Then Shecaniah the son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra, "We have acted unfaithfully against our God and have married foreign women from the peoples of the land; still, now there is hope for Israel concerning this.
verses.10:3: So now let us make a covenant with our God to send away all the wives and those born from them, by the counsel of the Lord and of those who tremble at the command of our God, and let it be done according to the law.
verses.10:4: Rise, for the matter rests on you, and we are with you. Be strong and act."
verses.10:5: Then Ezra rose and made the officials of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to act according to this word, and they swore.
verses.10:6: Then Ezra rose from in front of the house of God and went to the chamber of Jehohanan the son of Eliashib; and when he went there, he ate no bread and drank no water, for he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
verses.10:7: And they sent out a proclamation throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the people of the exile to gather at Jerusalem,
verses.10:8: and that, as for anyone who did not come within three days, according to the counsel of the officials and the elders, all his possessions would be confiscated, and he himself would be separated from the assembly of the exiles.
verses.10:9: So all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered at Jerusalem within the three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth of the month; and all the people sat in the open square of the house of God, trembling over the matter and from the rains.
verses.10:10: Then Ezra the priest rose and said to them, "You have acted unfaithfully and have married foreign women, adding to the guilt of Israel.
verses.10:11: So now offer confession to the LORD, the God of your fathers, and do His will; and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign women."
verses.10:12: Then all the assembly answered and said with a loud voice, "Indeed, it rests on us to act according to your word.
verses.10:13: However, the people are numerous, and this is a time of rains, and there is no strength to stand outside; and the work is not for one day or for two, for we have transgressed so greatly in this matter.
verses.10:14: Please let our officials stand for all the assembly, and let everyone in our cities who has married foreign women come at appointed times, and with them the elders of each city and its judges, until the burning anger of our God is turned away from us concerning this matter."
verses.10:15: Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah stood against this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.
verses.10:16: And the people of the exile did so. Then Ezra the priest and men who were ancestral heads, according to their fathers' houses, all of them by name, were set apart; and they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
verses.10:17: And they finished with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
verses.10:18: Now among the sons of the priests who had married foreign women there were found, from the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
verses.10:19: And they gave their hand to send away their wives, and being guilty, they brought a ram of the flock for their guilt.
verses.10:20: And from the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
verses.10:21: And from the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
verses.10:22: And from the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
verses.10:23: And from the Levites: Jozabad; Shimei; Kelaiah, that is, Kelita; Pethahiah; Judah; and Eliezer.
verses.10:24: And from the singers: Eliashib; and from the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
verses.10:25: And from Israel, from the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
verses.10:26: And from the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
verses.10:27: And from the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
verses.10:28: And from the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
verses.10:29: And from the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.
verses.10:30: And from the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
verses.10:31: And the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
verses.10:33: From the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
verses.10:34: From the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,
verses.10:43: From the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
verses.10:44: All these had taken foreign wives, and among them were wives who had borne children.

notes.1:4: "support him" translates the Piel of nasa (to lift up), which in Late Biblical Hebrew means to uphold, assist, or supply with material aid. "every survivor" renders the Niphal participle ha-nishar ("the one remaining"), used in post-exilic Hebrew for the surviving remnant of the exile.
notes.1:6: "in addition to everything that was offered freely" renders levad al-kol-hitnaddev, where the Hithpael perfect of nadav ("to volunteer, give freely") functions as an asyndetic relative clause after kol with impersonal passive force.
notes.1:9: Both agartal ("basin") and mahalafim ("knives") occur only here in the Hebrew Bible. Mahalafim is commonly connected with the root halaf ("to pierce, pass through") and Mishnaic Hebrew mahalaf ("slaughtering knife"), though some relate it to the sense "exchange" as "duplicates" or "replacement vessels."
notes.1:10: "secondary silver bowls" translates kefore kesef mishnim, where mishnim (plural of mishneh, "second" or "double") refers to bowls of a second sort or grade, or possibly double or matching bowls.
notes.1:11: The itemized counts in verses 9-10 total 2,499, whereas the Masoretic Text states 5,400 here, perhaps indicating that only the principal items were listed above or reflecting an early numerical divergence in transmission. The Hiphil he'elah ("brought up") pairs with the Niphal infinitive construct he'alot ("was brought up") from the same root alah.
notes.2:1: The written ketiv spells the king's name with an extra waw before the final resh (Nebuchadnezzor), while the read qere followed here is Nebuchadnezzar. Hebrew literally reads "the sons of the province," an idiom for the inhabitants of the Persian province of Judah.
notes.2:6: The preposition lamed ("of") specifies subdivisions within the clan of Pahath-moab, as also in 2:16 ("of Hezekiah"). Hebrew juxtaposes "Jeshua" and "Joab" without a conjunction (asyndeton), smoothly rendered "Jeshua and Joab."
notes.2:21: Beginning here, the census includes place names alongside family clans, alternating between Hebrew "sons of" (2:21, 24-26, 29, 33-35) and "men of" (2:22-23, 27-28). Both expressions denote residents or citizens associated with those towns.
notes.2:25: The Masoretic Text reads "Kiriath-arim," a shortened form of the town name "Kiriath-jearim" found in the parallel list at Nehemiah 7:29.
notes.2:43: Hebrew ha-netinim (from the root natan, "to give") literally means "the given ones," designating a hereditary class of servants assigned to temple duties (also in 2:58, 70).
notes.2:46: The written ketiv reads "Shamlai," while the read qere followed here transposes the middle consonants to "Shalmai."
notes.2:50: The written ketiv reads "Nephisim" (with yod), while the read qere followed here reads "Nephusim" (with waw).
notes.2:62: The Pual verb wayyego'alu (from ga'al II, "to defile") with the preposition "from" forms a pregnant construction meaning "they were disqualified as ceremonially unclean and excluded from the priesthood." Unlike Nehemiah 7:64 ("it was not found"), the Masoretic Text here uses the plural Niphal verb "they were not found."
notes.2:63: Hebrew ha-tirshata is an Old Persian official title designating the provincial governor of Judah.
notes.3:3: The clause rendered 'for dread was upon them' literally reads 'for in dread upon them' (Hebrew be'emah, a predicative use of the preposition beth). The Qere reads plural wayya'alu ('and they offered up', Hiphil of 'alah), whereas the Ketiv has singular wy'l ('and he offered up').
notes.3:10: The Masoretic Text vocalizes wayya'amidu as a transitive Hiphil ('they stationed', from 'amad) rather than an intransitive Qal ('the priests stood'). The phrase 'according to the order of' is literally 'by the hands of' ('al-yede).
notes.3:12: The clause 'when this house was founded before their eyes' translates a proleptic pronominal suffix on the Qal infinitive construct beyosdo (literally 'at its founding, this house, in their eyes'), a construction characteristic of Late Biblical Hebrew.
notes.4:2: The Qere reads welo ('and to Him'), matching the speakers' claim of worshipping Israel's God; the Ketiv reads wl' ('and not').
notes.4:4: The Qere reads umebahalim (Piel participle of bahal, 'terrifying/frightening'), whereas the Ketiv reads wmblhym (a metathesized form from balah, 'wearing down/troubling').
notes.4:8: The text of Ezra switches from Hebrew to Biblical Aramaic here (continuing through 6:18); 'chancellor' renders the official title be'el-te'em (literally 'master of decree').
notes.4:9: The Masoretic Text vocalizes all nine group names with Aramaic gentilic endings, though the first four may represent Persian official titles. Two Qere forms are followed here: 'Archevites' ('arkewaye' vs. Ketiv 'rkwy) and 'Dehaites' (dehaye' vs. Ketiv dhw', sometimes read as 'that is').
notes.4:12: The Qere reads weshurayya' shaklilu ('and they are completing the walls', Shaphel perfect of kll used inceptively or conatively in light of 4:13), whereas the Ketiv reads wshwry 'shkllw.
notes.4:13: 'In the end' translates the rare Old Persian loanword 'appetom (alternatively understood as 'revenue' or 'treasury'), paired with the Haphel verb tehanziq ('bring loss to', cf. 4:15, 22).
notes.5:1: The Qere reads nebiyya' ('the prophet', emphatic state with final aleph) for the Ketiv orthographic spelling nby'h; similar orthographic Ketiv/Qere variants occur in 5:12 and 5:15.
notes.5:3: The Aramaic noun 'ushsharna' ('structure', recurring in 5:9) is a loanword of uncertain origin, variously understood as 'structure', 'wall', or 'furnishings/woodwork'.
notes.5:4: The Masoretic Aramaic text reads first-person plural 'amarna' ('we spoke'), preserved literally here rather than harmonized to third-person plural ('they said') as in the Septuagint and Syriac.
notes.5:8: 'Massive stones' translates Aramaic 'eben gelal (literally 'stone of rolling', referring to heavy ashlar blocks moved on rollers), and 'diligently' renders the Persian loanword 'osparna'.
notes.6:3: Aramaic mesobelin is a Poel passive participle of the root sbl ("bear, support"), understood here of foundations being solidly laid or retained.
notes.6:4: MT reads hadat ("new"), describing fresh timber; the Septuagint reflects had ("one"), as in "one course of timber."
notes.6:6: Aramaic apharsekhaye is an Old Persian administrative title meaning "investigators" or "officials," traditionally transliterated as "Apharsachites." MT also reads the third-person suffix "their colleagues" before shifting to second-person address.
notes.6:17: Following the Qere lehatta'ah ("for a sin offering", singular emphatic); the Ketiv writes lhty', a variant spelling or plural ("for sin offerings").
notes.6:22: MT literally reads "the king of Assyria," a traditional designation here applied to the Persian king Darius as successor to the earlier Mesopotamian empires.
notes.7:9: Hebrew yesud is a rare construct noun from the root ysd ("found, establish"), literally "the beginning of the ascent/going up."
notes.7:12: Aramaic gemir (Peil passive participle of gmr, "complete") is widely understood as an abbreviated epistolary salutation ("full greetings" or "complete peace"), though it may alternatively mean "accomplished" modifying "scribe."
notes.7:18: Following the Qere forms 'alak ("to you") and 'ehak ("your brothers"); the Ketiv writes both with an older medial yod ('lyk, 'hyk) without change in sense.
notes.7:25: Following the Qere dayenin ("judging", Peal active participle of dyn); the Ketiv writes d'nyn with an aleph glide, a standard Aramaic hollow-verb spelling.
notes.7:26: Following the Qere lishroshi (Ketiv lshrshw), an abstract noun from the root shrsh ("uproot") denoting "uprooting" or "banishment" from the community.
notes.8:3: In the Masoretic Text, 'From the sons of Shecaniah' opens verse 3 without a named leader; it appears to specify the Davidic lineage of Hattush at the end of 8:2 (cf. 1 Chr 3:22). Similarly, MT omits a separate ancestral clan name before Shecaniah in 8:5 and before Shelomith in 8:10.
notes.8:14: Following the qere 'Zaccur' (ketiv reads 'Zabbud'). The Masoretic Text also reads the singular suffix 'with him' despite the two names preceding it.
notes.8:17: Following the qere forms 'I commanded' (Piel of tsavah; ketiv reads 'I sent out', Hiphil of yatsa) and 'the temple servants' (Hebrew ha-netinim, literally 'the given ones'; ketiv reads the Qal passive participle ha-netunim). MT also points the singular 'his brother' without a conjunction before 'the temple servants.'
notes.8:24: MT prefixes the preposition le- to Sherebiah without a conjunction, which may introduce Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten kinsmen as a second group of twelve Levites alongside the twelve priests (cf. 8:18-19, 30) or list them in apposition.
notes.8:25: Following the qere spelling of 'I weighed out' (Qal of shaqal; the ketiv is an orthographic variant with vav). The verb 'had contributed' (Hiphil of rum) uses the prefixed definite article as a relative marker, a feature of Late Biblical Hebrew.
notes.9:5: 'My fasting' translates the Hebrew hapax legomenon ta'anit, derived from the root 'anah ('humble/afflict oneself', cf. 8:21), denoting self-humbling or fasting. 'With my garment and my cloak torn' renders the Hebrew preposition be- with the Qal infinitive construct of qara' ('in my tearing').
notes.9:8: The noun techinnah usually means 'supplication for favor,' but here (as in Josh 11:20) denotes 'favor' shown by God. In 'so that our God may give light to our eyes,' 'our God' functions syntactically as the subject of the Hiphil infinitive construct of 'or ('give light').
notes.9:13: Literally 'You have held back below our iniquity' (Qal of chasak, 'hold back, spare'), an elliptical idiom meaning that God restrained His judgment to less than their iniquity deserved.
notes.10:2: The verb translated "married" here and in 10:10, 14, 17, and 18 is the Hiphil of yashav (literally "cause to dwell" or "bring home"), a Late Biblical Hebrew idiom for taking wives. For "Elam," the qere reads Elam while the ketiv spells it Olam.
notes.10:3: The Masoretic vocalization reads Adonai ("the Lord"), whereas some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions point the word Adoni ("my lord"), referring to Ezra.
notes.10:16: The Masoretic Text reads a Niphal plural verb ("were set apart") with Ezra and the ancestral heads as compound subject, whereas a proposed emendation reads a Hiphil singular ("he selected"). The form ledaryosh ("to investigate") is an unusual spelling of the Qal infinitive construct of darash.
notes.10:19: Literally "and being guilty, a ram of the flock for their guilt," with the verb ("brought" or "offered") implied after the plural adjective ashemim ("guilty").
notes.10:44: For "had taken," the qere reads the Qal perfect plural nas'u in place of the ketiv form. The second clause (literally "and there were among them wives, and they produced children") is difficult in the Masoretic Text and is translated as written rather than emended from 1 Esdras 9:36.
